name: Bald copes

card.summary: Humorous reassurances balding men tell themselves and each other, such as that baldness signals dominance, framing hair loss as acceptable and a head shave as a deliberate look.

quick.overview:
"Bald copes" are jokes and reassurances about hair loss, often posted by balding men. Examples include that a shaved head looks dominant or that bald men are seen as confident.

They connect to how men adapt to pattern hair loss: some seek treatment, others shave their heads and lean into the look. Research shows attitudes toward balding vary by culture.
quick.how: Shared in forums and conversation as humor and mutual support, they accompany choices such as shaving the head, keeping short hair or trying treatments.
quick.risks: The statements themselves carry no health risk. Pattern hair loss can lower body-image satisfaction for some people, and medical treatments exist for those who want them.

lead: Bald copes are humorous coping statements made by balding men about hair loss. Pattern hair loss affects roughly half of men by age 50, and Wikipedia describes it as a moderately stressful condition that lowers body-image satisfaction for some, though most men cope and keep their sense of self [1].

Views on bald men differ across studies: a 2001 South Korean study found most people rated balding men as less attractive, while a 2002 survey of Welsh women found bald and gray-haired men appealing, and one theory holds that shaving the head signals dominance or status [1].

chain: Man chooses a shaved or short style
angle.text: These statements help men adopt a shaved or short style with confidence rather than treating hair loss as something to hide.

paras: Male pattern baldness is often seen as a sign of aging, so some men shave their heads rather than seek treatment [2].
No studies found on the statements themselves; the attitude surveys above concern perceptions of balding men [1].
